difficulty_calibration.notes: Perfectly calibrated for an ESAT Section 1 question. It tests a fundamental concept with a classic, high-frequency trap.

selectivity_audit.main_trap: The 'diameter vs area' trap: students often forget to square the diameter scaling factor, leading to the common error of treating resistance as inversely proportional to diameter (1/2) rather than area (1/4).
selectivity_audit.why_not_plug_and_chug: No numerical values for resistivity or absolute dimensions are provided; the student must perform symbolic proportional reasoning.
selectivity_audit.expected_mid_student_error: Selecting B (3/2 R) by failing to square the diameter factor.

notes: This is an exemplary ESAT question. It is concise, relies on a single core physical principle, and uses a well-defined trap to discriminate between students who understand the geometry of the resistance formula and those who do not.
